notes: Line forms: {n} Feyre's narration, first person past tense, shown in italics; {s,e,t} a line spoken aloud (speaker, portrait expression, text); {hint} a game tip on its own card; {choices:[{t,goto,do}]}; {do:[actions]}; {goto}. Any line or choice may carry if_flag, if_not_flag, if_item, if_not_item or if_chapter. Wording is written for the game; the few short book lines kept are listed in quotes.json.

lines.n: Paper in one hand and a pen in the other, I crept through the sleeping house, marking doors and windows and stairs with crosses and circles. I couldn't write more than my letters. My map would mean nothing to anyone else.
If I was going to live here, I would learn this house so well I could find my way out of it blind.
A breeze stirred the moonlight in the hall. The garden doors opened, and he came in.
I'd forgotten how huge he was like this. Curled horns, a wolf's face, a bear's bulk moving like a cat. He was limping. Dark, shining stains followed him across the marble.
A blinding flash, and he stood before me. His clothes hung in long, vicious slashes, though the skin beneath was smooth. But his hand dripped blood onto the floor. That wound wasn't closing.

lines.t: Did you kill it? The Bogge?
Yes.

lines.n: Flat. Empty. As if he'd had to go somewhere very deep inside himself to do it, and hadn't come all the way back.

lines.t: You're hurt.

lines.n: He looked down at his hand as if he'd forgotten he had one. Then at the paper on the table.

lines.t: What's that?
I thought I should learn my way around.
You can't write, can you.
No wonder you got so good at other things.

choices.t: Offer to see to his hand.

lines.n: I picked up my map and made it as far as the stairs. Drip. Drip. I turned back.

lines.t: Where can we clean that hand?
There's a small infirmary.

lines.n: It was more cupboard than sickroom. Immortals didn't need much more. His skin burned against my cold fingers. I braced for the claws to come out the whole time I cleaned and bound the cuts. They never did.

lines.t: You can't write. And yet you taught yourself to hunt, to survive. How?
That's what happens when other lives depend on yours. You do what you have to.
You aren't what I expected. For a human.

lines.n: He didn't say good night. Neither did I.

By morning the marble had been washed clean. I meant to spend the quiet hour looking at the paintings at last, but voices came from the dining room, low and tense. I slid into the shadow behind the door.

lines.t: Tell me what you're playing at. Time's running out, Tam, and you're brooding. You've stopped even trying.
It was wrong from the beginning. I can't do it. Not after the way my father treated humans. I won't become him.

And doom the rest of us? I stayed because I had hope, not to watch you trip over your own conscience. That lump of stone you carry where a heart should be has gone very soft lately. The Bogge walked our lands, Tam! The borders between the courts have fallen, and our woods are filling up with filth like the puca.
Careful. Do you think I can't see what's happening in my own court? What I could lose? What's gone already?

lines.n: The air throbbed, and the metal tang of magic filled my nose. I leaned closer. My finger knocked softly against the door.
A human wouldn't have heard it. Both of them whirled.

lines.t: Morning. Going for a ride, Lucien?
Not today. Tam will go with you.

lines.n: He patted my shoulder on his way out, looking far too pleased with himself.

lines.t: Another time, human.
Whenever you want to go, say so.
I don't want to go hunting. I hate hunting.
Then what do you want to do?

lines.n: He walked me through the sunlit halls. The roses outside the open windows scented everything.

lines.t: You've been riding out to hunt, and you don't even like it. No wonder the two of you never catch anything.
How's your hand?
I never said thank you. A wound from the Bogge heals too slowly to save us; that's how it kills. So, thank you. The hand still works.
I had to be able to draw a bowstring the next day. You learn.
Has anyone ever looked after you?
No.

lines.n: I'd stopped feeling sorry for myself about that a long time ago.

lines.t: Tell me something. Do you plan to use that knife you took from my table, or just carry it around?
How did you know?

I was trained to notice. But mostly I could smell the fear on you. If you want to stand a chance of escaping my kind, you'll need better ideas than dinner knives. Though with your gift for listening at doors, you may learn something useful yet.

lines.n: My ears burned. But there was no point pretending.

lines.t: Lucien said there wasn't much time. Time for what? Will more things like the Bogge come here?
I'm immortal, Feyre. Time is all I have. Whatever's plaguing our lands will pass someday, if the Cauldron's kind. But yes. Now that the Bogge got in, I'd expect others to follow.

lines.n: At the end of the hall, he pushed open two tall doors.

lines.t: As requested. The library.
